name: @asolens/mcp

tools.name: find_app
tools.description: Looks up an app by id, App Store URL, or name and returns candidate matches with rating and developer info.

query.description: App name or search text to look up on the App Store.

country.description: Two-letter App Store storefront country code, e.g. "us". Defaults to the server's configured default country.

limit.description: Maximum matches to return for a name search (max 200, Apple's own ceiling). Ignored when query is a numeric id or App Store URL.

tools.name: app_snapshot
tools.description: Resolves an app by id, App Store URL, or name and returns its current listing data plus the developer's other apps in this storefront.

app.description: App to resolve: a numeric App Store id, an App Store URL, or an app name.

country.description: Two-letter App Store storefront country code, e.g. "us". Defaults to the server's configured default country.

tools.name: search_ranks
tools.description: Ranked apps for one keyword in one country, as the App Store lists them (fetched from this machine; cached for the UTC day). Bundles are kept as ranked rows. resultCount is what Apple returned (250 is a ceiling), not how many apps compete.

keyword.description: Search keyword to rank apps for. Accents matter: Apple usually treats an accented and an unaccented spelling as different searches, and neither is reliably better (br 'jogos de matemática' ranked #19 where 'jogos de matematica' was unranked; mx 'juegos de matematicas' #20 where 'juegos de matemáticas' was #74). Sometimes it returns identical results for both, and nothing observable predicts which case you are in, so in a non-English storefront always run both spellings rather than guessing. Note that Swedish å/ä/ö are letters, not accents -- 'för' and 'for' are different words, not two spellings of one.

country.description: Two-letter App Store storefront country code, e.g. "us". Defaults to the server's configured default country.

top.description: How many ranked entries to return, most-relevant first (max 250 — the ceiling Apple's search returns).

tools.name: keyword_ranks
tools.description: Looks up where one app ranks for a list of keywords, in one or more storefronts, with day-over-day trend where available.

app.description: App to check: a numeric App Store id, an App Store URL, or an app name.

pairs.description: Explicit keyword/country pairs instead of the keywords x countries cross product. Use this whenever the storefronts need different keywords: 13 Brazilian plus 9 Nordic terms is 22 rows here, against 198 mostly-nonsense pairs as a cross product. Rows come back in the order given. Cannot be combined with keywords/countries.

keywords.description: Keywords to check this app's rank for (max 50; keywords x countries must not exceed 25 pairs total). Accents matter: Apple usually treats an accented and an unaccented spelling as different searches, and neither is reliably better (br 'jogos de matemática' ranked #19 where 'jogos de matematica' was unranked; mx 'juegos de matematicas' #20 where 'juegos de matemáticas' was #74). Sometimes it returns identical results for both, and nothing observable predicts which case you are in, so in a non-English storefront always run both spellings rather than guessing. Note that Swedish å/ä/ö are letters, not accents -- 'för' and 'for' are different words, not two spellings of one.

countries.description: Storefront country codes to check, up to 8, paired with every entry in `keywords`. Defaults to the server's configured default country. Keywords x countries must not exceed 25 pairs total.

variants.description: For every keyword with an accent on a Latin, Greek or Cyrillic letter, ALSO look up the stripped spelling and return the two side by side in one row, with identicalResults saying whether Apple actually answered one query for both (null when BOTH spellings returned nothing -- there was no list to compare, which is not the same as the lists matching). Turn this on whenever a keyword has an accent: the difference is sometimes nothing and sometimes decisive (br 'tabuada de multiplicação' #12 vs 'tabuada de multiplicacao' #114; 'jogos de matemática' #19 vs the plain form not returned at all), and nothing observable predicts which -- checking one spelling alone can make a live keyword look dead. Each variant counts against the 25 keyword-country pair cap. Only strips accents, never adds them: if you already have the plain spelling, pass the accented one explicitly to compare. Marks that are part of the word (Devanagari vowel signs, kana dakuten, Thai tone marks) are not accents and get no variant.

coverage.description: For YOUR OWN app (App Store Connect credentials required), report which of each keyword's words actually appear in the text Apple indexes -- name, subtitle and the keywords field, checked together rather than field by field. This is the one thing you can change, and no public endpoint exposes the keywords field. Silently absent for anyone else's app, or with no credentials configured. Coverage is an observation about text, NOT a ranking model: a missing word does not prove the app cannot rank (Apple stems and matches in ways nobody outside Apple can enumerate) and full coverage does not promise it will. Where the listing runs words together without spaces (Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Korean compounds), a word that may sit inside such a run comes back covered: null -- cannot tell -- rather than missing.

depth.description: Add autocompleteDepth (how many App Store autocomplete suggestions begin with the keyword) to each row, and to each variant when variants is on. Free, works in every storefront, and adds no wall-clock. It caps at 10 and a 0 means nothing popular extends the string -- NOT that nobody searches it.

tools.name: compare_queries
tools.description: Runs two keywords in one storefront and reports how much their ranked results overlap. Use this BEFORE concluding anything from a rank difference between two queries: rank is relative to whoever else is in that result set, so an app at #19 for one phrase and #131 for another has not necessarily been hurt by the extra word -- the two searches may simply have different competitors. identicalResults: true means Apple answered one query for both (it does this for some accented/unaccented pairs, and for some rewordings), so any rank difference is noise; NULL means both queries returned nothing, so there was no list to compare and no conclusion to draw either way. A low overlap means the two are genuinely different searches and their ranks are not comparable at all.

b.description: Second search keyword, the one to compare against.

country.description: Two-letter App Store storefront country code, e.g. "us". Defaults to the server's configured default country.

app.description: Optional app (id, URL, or name) to also report the rank of in each result set, so you can see the rank difference and the overlap that qualifies it together.

top.description: How deep to compare the two ranked lists (default 25). identicalResults always compares the FULL lists, not just this depth.

tools.name: my_listing
tools.description: Reads YOUR OWN app's indexed listing text -- name, subtitle and the keywords field -- from App Store Connect, per locale. This is the only way to see the keywords field: it is private to the developer and no public endpoint exposes it, so for anyone else's app it stays unavailable. Requires App Store Connect API credentials; without them the tool says so rather than failing. Use it before judging a keyword: coverage of a query's words across name+subtitle+keywords is what you can actually change.

app.description: Your app: a numeric App Store id, an App Store URL, or a bundle id. It must be an app your App Store Connect API key can see.

country.description: Two-letter storefront country code. Given, the response leads with the locale that storefront serves (and says so when the app has no localization for it and falls back). Omitted, every locale is returned.

tools.name: audit_keywords
tools.description: Tests every word in YOUR OWN keywords field by searching a phrase where that word is the distinguishing one -- an anchor your app certainly covers, plus the word under test ('matemática' + 'escola'). Ranking for the probe means the word is working; not ranking means it is not earning its 100 characters. Searching each word alone instead would mostly measure how small your app is. READ THE SUMMARY FIRST: if almost nothing ranks, the answer is usually not 'fix these words' -- a live audit found 1 of 19 German probes ranking, with the app at zero ratings against competitors holding thousands, which means keyword work is not the lever in that storefront at all. Requires App Store Connect credentials (the keywords field is private).

app.description: Your app: numeric App Store id, App Store URL, or bundle id. Must be visible to the configured App Store Connect key.

country.description: Storefront to test in, e.g. "br". Defaults to the server's configured default country. The keyword field tested is the one for the locale that storefront serves.

anchor.description: The context word each probe is built from. Omitted, one is picked from your app name and reported back as anchorSource: "auto" -- check it. A mechanical anchor can produce a phrase no human would type, which gives a strange result set and a confidently wrong answer; the category word a user would actually search is usually better.

probes.description: Override the generated probe for specific words, e.g. {word: "contar", probe: "aprender a contar"} where natural phrasing beats "<anchor> contar". Words not listed here still use the anchor.

word.description: A word from your keyword field.

probe.description: The exact phrase to search for it.

suggestions.description: Include, per word, what App Store autocomplete says people typing that word are actually looking for. Free, adds no measurable wall-clock (autocomplete has its own request lane), and works in all 17 storefronts -- unlike search volume, which no source sells outside the us. READ IT: rank cannot tell you a word attracts the wrong audience. Measured live in se, the best-ranking word in a field turned out to return Swedish football-league tables. Pass false only to shrink the payload.

tools.name: compare_markets
tools.description: Runs the keyword-field audit across several storefronts at once and puts them side by side: how much of your keyword field places in each, your rating count there, and the competitor median with its sample size. This is the 'which market should I work on' question, which no single-market answer can settle. Uses auto-picked anchors only -- to override an anchor or a probe, run audit_keywords for that one market. Requires App Store Connect credentials (the keywords field is private). READ THE ANCHOR COLUMN: each market's numbers come from a different anchor in a different language, so the medians are NOT commensurable and only large differences mean anything.

app.description: Your app: numeric App Store id, App Store URL, or bundle id. Must be visible to the configured App Store Connect key.

countries.description: Storefronts to compare, up to 8. Each costs roughly one App Store search per word in that locale's keyword field (free, but a four-market comparison takes about half a minute).

anchors.description: Per-market anchor overrides, e.g. {country: 'jp', anchor: '算数'}. Markets not listed pick one automatically. Worth setting wherever you know the category term a person there would actually search: the auto anchor is mechanical, and a phrase nobody types asks a different question.

probes.description: Per-market probe overrides, e.g. {country: 'br', word: 'soma', probe: 'soma e subtração'}. This is where market knowledge pays: measured in br, natural phrasing put words at #23 and #35 that mechanical probes put at #118 and #105, moving the market from 1 of 11 to 3 of 11.

tools.name: snapshot_save
tools.description: Captures a named, kept measurement of a keyword set: rank (including null, which is a value here), resultCount, the top 10 app ids, keyword coverage with the listing version it was read from, and your rating count against the competitor median per storefront. Take one BEFORE shipping a metadata change -- the moment cannot be recovered afterwards, because Apple publishes no rank history and this tool's own cache is per-UTC-day. Label each keyword ('target', 'control', 'regression watch') so a later diff can tell signal from drift: if the controls move while nothing about them changed, the reading is noise.

name.description: Name to save under, e.g. "pre-release-2026-08-29". Re-using a name overwrites that snapshot.

app.description: The app to record ranks for: numeric App Store id, App Store URL, or name.

keywords.description: Keywords to capture in every one of `countries` (a cross product). Use `pairs` instead when different storefronts need different keywords. Keywords x countries must not exceed 60.

label.description: Free text, e.g. "target", "control", "regression watch". Never interpreted -- it only groups the diff.

countries.description: Storefronts to capture in, paired with every entry in `keywords`. Defaults to the server's configured default country.

pairs.description: Explicit keyword/country pairs, instead of the keywords x countries cross product. Use this whenever storefronts need different keyword sets -- 13 Brazilian plus 9 Nordic keywords is 22 rows here, against 198 mostly-nonsense pairs as a cross product, and it keeps one baseline in ONE snapshot instead of splitting it into two that must both be remembered at diff time. Cannot be combined with keywords/countries.

tools.name: snapshot_diff
tools.description: Compares two named snapshots keyword by keyword: rank before and after (null included), how the result set size changed, which apps entered or left the top 10, and your ratings against the competitor median on each date. Rows are grouped by the labels given when saving. READ THE CONTROLS FIRST: if keywords you expected to hold still have moved, the whole comparison is drift and the targets prove nothing. Deliberately reports no significance or confidence -- with small numbers there is no statistical power, and a confidence label would be theatre.

tools.name: niche_report
tools.description: Builds a competitive report across a set of keywords: the union of top-ranked apps, a weakness score per competitor, difficulty per keyword, and gaps for your own app.

keywords.description: Keywords defining the niche (max 30). Accents matter: Apple usually treats an accented and an unaccented spelling as different searches, and neither is reliably better (br 'jogos de matemática' ranked #19 where 'jogos de matematica' was unranked; mx 'juegos de matematicas' #20 where 'juegos de matemáticas' was #74). Sometimes it returns identical results for both, and nothing observable predicts which case you are in, so in a non-English storefront always run both spellings rather than guessing. Note that Swedish å/ä/ö are letters, not accents -- 'för' and 'for' are different words, not two spellings of one.

country.description: Two-letter App Store storefront country code, e.g. "us". Defaults to the server's configured default country.

app.description: Your own app, to compare against competitors and compute gaps: id, URL, or name.

name.description: Name for this niche; required (together with save: true) to save it for later reuse.

top.description: How many top-ranked apps per keyword to include in the report.

save.description: If true, saves this niche definition for later reuse -- requires name to also be given, otherwise nothing is saved (see saved/savedReason in the response).

include_inputs.description: If true, every modelled value (weakness, difficulty, ownTrend, volume) also includes the raw inputs it was computed from. Default false keeps kind, value and model -- far smaller for reports with many keywords/apps, while still saying which model produced each number (ASOLens's own scoring vs DataForSEO's volume estimate).

volume.description: DataForSEO's Apple keyword dataset covers the 'us' storefront ONLY -- in every other storefront volume comes back unavailable saying exactly that, at no cost and without failing the call. Look up keyword search volume via DataForSEO (paid, per the server's configured credentials) for these keywords, plus discoveredKeywords (the top 10 higher-volume terms the competitor apps rank for that aren't in this keyword list). When no DataForSEO credentials are configured, or this is false, volume is unavailable with a fix -- no error, no partial failure. Two-stage cost: an app's top-50 window caches per app/country/UTC day (free on repeat), but a keyword the window misses is then searched BY NAME across the app's full list -- one extra $0.012 per 150 missed per app, even when the window is cached today. Still unpriced after that full search means none of the queried apps ranks for it; window-only-checked means just that -- neither implies low demand.

depth.description: Fetch App Store autocomplete for each keyword and report autocompleteDepth: how many suggested queries begin with that keyword. Free, works in every storefront (unlike volume, which is 'us'-only), and adds no wall-clock on a cold call because autocomplete uses a separate request lane from search. READ IT CAREFULLY: Apple's autocomplete is prefix completion, so this counts popular queries that EXTEND the keyword, not searches for the keyword itself. It caps at 10, so it cannot rank head terms ('cool math games' at 316,880 searches and 'math games for kids' at 1,109 both score 10). A 0 means nothing popular extends the string -- NOT that nobody searches the phrase ('math quiz for kids' scores 0 and is plainly a real search). Treat a low score as a prompt to look closer, never as proof a keyword is dead.

tools.name: low_star_reviews
tools.description: Fetches recent low-star reviews for an app so you can read what's actually bothering users; theme extraction is left to the caller.

app.description: App to fetch reviews for: a numeric App Store id, an App Store URL, or an app name.

country.description: Two-letter App Store storefront country code, e.g. "us". Defaults to the server's configured default country.

maxStars.description: Only include reviews with this star rating or lower.

limit.description: Maximum number of reviews to return.

tools.name: suggest_keywords
tools.description: Returns App Store autocomplete suggestions for a search term, showing what people actually search for -- the way to check a keyword's intent is what you assume (e.g. 'rakna' autocompleting to calorie counting, not maths). Suggestion order is Apple's own ranking. Autocomplete is PREFIX completion, so a count of zero means nothing popular extends the term -- NOT that nobody searches it ('math quiz for kids' returns none and is plainly a real search). Read a low count as a prompt to look closer, never as proof a keyword is dead. This tool never spends money. It cannot buy search volume (no vendor prices a bare App Store keyword), but a suggestion that a niche_report, keyword_table or price_keywords run already bought a price for in 'us', on any of the last 7 UTC days (today counted as the first), comes back priced for free in `volumes`, carrying the day the price was bought so an older number says it is older; when none of the suggestions has such a price, a single `volume` field says why.

term.description: Search term to get App Store autocomplete suggestions for.

country.description: Two-letter App Store storefront country code, e.g. "us". Defaults to the server's configured default country.

tools.name: price_keywords
tools.description: Looks up DataForSEO search volume for keywords you already have, by naming each one to the vendor. Use this to RANK a list -- 'which of these 40 terms is biggest' -- which niche_report cannot answer, because it reads each competitor's top 50 keywords only and everything below that comes back unpriced. This asks across each app's full ranked list instead. Paid: keywords are sent in batches of 150, and each batch is $0.012 per app, plus $0.00012 per keyword actually found -- so 200 keywords across 2 apps is 4 batches, about $0.05. Free for the rest of the UTC day once bought. US storefront only, like all volume in this server. A keyword still comes back unavailable if none of the queried apps ranks for it -- volume exists only as 'the keywords this app ranks for', so the answer depends on which competitors are reached, and it is NEVER evidence a keyword is unpopular.

keywords.description: The keywords to price. Duplicates and casing are normalised.

country.description: Two-letter App Store storefront country code. Volume is "us"-only; any other storefront returns unavailable at no cost.

apps.description: Competitor app ids to price through. STRONGLY PREFERRED: supplying these makes the call cost ZERO App Store requests. Leave empty and the tool searches the App Store for a few of your keywords to find competitors, which is rate-limited.

max_apps.description: How many competitor apps to query. Cost is per app AND per 150-keyword batch: $0.012 x ceil(keywords/150) x apps, so 100 keywords at 2 apps is $0.024 before per-keyword charges. Each app reaches a different ranked-keyword list, so more apps means more keywords priced.

tools.name: keyword_table
tools.description: Builds a table of your saved keywords with current rank, difficulty and trend, refreshing today's data by default.

country.description: Two-letter App Store storefront country code, e.g. "us". Defaults to the server's configured default country.

app.description: Your own app, to compute rank/trend against in the table: id, URL, or name.

refresh.description: Re-fetch today's rank data for each saved keyword that hasn't been refreshed yet today, before building the table. Keywords already refreshed today are served from cache for free; up to 20 newly-fetched keywords per call count against the cap, so repeated calls eventually cover every saved keyword.

add.description: Keywords to save before building the table (max 50 - each triggers a live App Store search when refresh is true, which it is by default).

notes.description: Notes to attach to already-saved keywords, applied before the table is built.

keyword.description: A previously saved keyword to annotate.

notes.description: Note text to store for this keyword. null leaves the existing note unchanged (it does not clear it); pass an empty string to clear it.

volume.description: DataForSEO's Apple keyword dataset covers the 'us' storefront ONLY -- in every other storefront volume comes back unavailable saying exactly that, at no cost and without failing the call. Look up keyword search volume via DataForSEO (paid, per the server's configured credentials). When no DataForSEO credentials are configured, or this is false, volume is unavailable with a fix -- no error, no partial failure. Two-stage cost: an app's top-50 window caches per app/country/UTC day (free on repeat), but a keyword the window misses is then searched BY NAME across the app's full list -- one extra $0.012 per 150 missed per app, even when the window is cached today. Still unpriced after that full search means none of the queried apps ranks for it; window-only-checked means just that -- neither implies low demand.

depth.description: Fetch App Store autocomplete for each keyword and report autocompleteDepth: how many suggested queries begin with that keyword. Free, works in every storefront (unlike volume, which is 'us'-only), and adds no wall-clock on a cold call because autocomplete uses a separate request lane from search. READ IT CAREFULLY: Apple's autocomplete is prefix completion, so this counts popular queries that EXTEND the keyword, not searches for the keyword itself.
